desc:
Given a string s of lowercase letters and an integer k, return the length of the longest substring that contains at most k different characters.

s = "eceba", k = 2
"ece" has two distinct characters
result = 3

If k = 0 no non-empty substring qualifies, so the answer is 0.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Try every start and extend until the substring has too many distinct letters. That is O(n²) at least. Can the start pointer avoid going back?
If a window has more than k distinct characters, every longer window that contains it does too. So you only ever need to move the left end forward.
Keep a count per character inside the window and the number of characters with a non-zero count. When that number exceeds k, remove characters from the left until it is back to k.
editorial: Maintain a window [left, right] and a frequency table of its characters. Add s[right]; if the number of distinct characters becomes larger than k, shrink the window from the left, decrementing counts and dropping a character from the table when its count reaches zero. After the window is valid again, its length is a candidate for the answer.

Validity is monotone: any substring of a valid window is also valid, so the smallest valid left end never moves backward. Each index is added once and removed at most once, giving O(n) time. The table has at most k + 1 entries, so the space is O(min(n, k)).
